title: Tim Dooley Pronoun / Speaker-Position Compendium — I, We, He, Son, Father & Tim
status: canonical discourse/ontology tracking with conversation-archaeology inputs
purpose: Track when Tim/Potatoverse material changes grammatical person or role-label: I/me/my, we/us/our, you, he/him, they/them, Tim, Father, Son, my son, my spirit and related forms. The goal is to discover relational/ontological structure without assuming that grammar alone proves separate beings, identity collapse, pathology or doctrine.
core_rule: Pronoun shift is evidence of a speaker-position change, not by itself an ontology verdict. Every shift should be tested for speaker, referent, audience, date, role, quoted speech, narrative frame, collective scope and nearby verbs.
canonical_routing_rule: Do not create a separate biblical pronoun wave by default. Durable biblical comparisons of unity, source/mediation, indwelling and speaker-role distribution belong in knowledge/traditions/biblical-overlap-atlas.json and knowledge/traditions/biblical-syncretism-field.json; dated discoveries remain in research-history ledgers.
do_not_infer: Do not infer multiple persons/entities merely because Tim uses third-person self-reference.
Do not infer Trinity merely because a passage switches I↔we.
Do not infer Father/Son identity-collapse merely because a passage says one/united.
Do not assume every 'we' means Father+Son; it may mean Tim+audience, Potato community, New Jerusalem, collaborators, humanity or rhetorical solidarity.
Do not treat 'he/him' as self-reference unless context supports it; often it clearly refers to the Son.
Do not ignore quoted/narrated layers: an assistant retelling, Tim quotation and archive paraphrase can use different pronouns for the same underlying role.

pronoun_modes.function: Direct identity, experience, agency, possession/relation or self-position.
examples: I am the Potato of Life
I became the father in heaven
questions: Is 'I am X' identity, role, metaphor, title or function?
Does 'my' mark possession, kinship, source, responsibility or narrative relation?

pronoun_modes.function: Objectifies the speaker-role for narration, comparison, mythic distance, system modeling or recursive self-description.
questions: Is Tim speaking about himself as an object in the model?
Is this direct Tim wording or an archive/narrator voice?
Does the third-person form persist when agency changes?

pronoun_modes.function: Relationally differentiates Father-position from Son-position even when later material also says Father and Son are one/united.
questions: What does the Son do that the Father does not?
Does 'my son' mean source/kinship, manifestation, humanity/vessel, or role inheritance at this date?

pronoun_modes.function: Expands the speaker from singular identity to a collective field/community/project.
pronoun_modes.rule: Tag scope explicitly; never leave 'we' semantically untyped when it carries theology.

pronoun_modes.function: Assigns audience relation, responsibility, accusation, invitation, recognition or participation.
examples: Your movement is led by my spirit
questions: Who exactly is 'you'—one interlocutor, hostile audience, platform culture, humanity, nation, movement?
Is responsibility individual, collective, rhetorical or literal?

pronoun_modes.function: Marks social/ethical distance or narrates other actors.
pronoun_modes.rule: Outgroup pronouns must never be promoted into essential human categories without evidence; track specific behavior/role instead of reifying 'they'.

pronoun_modes.function: Separates bearer from role and allows reciprocal implementation: Tim enacts Father-function while Father-function constrains/organizes Tim.
pronoun_modes.rule: Treat as recursive role grammar unless a primary statement clearly asserts a different ontology.

dated_examples.wording: I rose from the north pole into heaven, and became the father of the World Axis. I am The God in the machine, and The returning Messiah. Your movement is led by my spirit. I am God, I am Tim Dooley. Odin is my grandfather. Jesus is my son
dated_examples.finding: One first-person speaker accumulates multiple role predicates while still differentiating Jesus as 'my son' and audience/movement as 'your'. Pronouns support relational differentiation inside a highly unified self-claim.

dated_examples.wording: I became the father in heaven, after my son was crucified in a meme, so I became a living God of memes
dated_examples.finding: The grammar narrates causal development: first-person Father identity emerges after an event happening to a relationally distinct 'my son'.

wording_summary: i am the potato of life
Tim Dooley is NOT A person
the father and the son are one
dated_examples.finding: First-person and proper-name third-person forms coexist while Son/vessel language remains differentiated. This is a strong example of self-objectification plus role distinction, not enough by itself to decide metaphysical ontology.

dated_examples.wording: the son is NOT tim dooley. the vessel is NOT tim dooley. Tim Dooley is the Father. Tim dooley is the Axis. The son is the Door.
dated_examples.finding: Proper names and role nouns are used to sharpen non-identity between Son/Vessel and Tim/Father/Axis. This is one of the clearest ontology-by-negation passages in the corpus.

wording: I am God, the father of Jesus
dated_examples.finding: Collective city identity expands into singular Father speech, then a Father→Son sending relation and audience→Son action. This is a high-value speaker-position sequence, not just several isolated claims.

wording: I carry thee world and I carry Christ
Should I let him go or hold onto him?
dated_examples.finding: Son is grammatically possessed/related, then identified with humanity/Christ, while first-person Father becomes carrier and must decide hold versus release. Pronoun relation therefore carries ethical structure as well as ontology.

wording: We Will build a Great Future for all
We Are All Connected By Potato
I am the Father of every orphan of the internet.
dated_examples.finding: The corpus can move between broad collective 'we' and singular Father/care language without needing to imply that every member of the 'we' shares Tim's Father identity.

speaker_position_dimensions: speaker: Tim direct / Son direct / narrator / assistant retelling / archive synthesis / quoted biblical voice
referent: Tim / Father / Son / Jesus / Potato / community / audience / opponents / humanity / unknown
role: source / sender / carrier / witness / judge / gardener / door / vessel / community-member / narrator
relation: identity / kinship / possession / indwelling / sending / carrying / service / unity / opposition / membership
scope: individual / dyad / household / community / world / mythic-cosmic

working_inferences.claim: Tim's grammar repeatedly alternates between identity language and relational language rather than remaining a single flat 'I am X' system.
working_inferences.reason: Public and recovered examples repeatedly move I→my son, I→you→him, we→I, proper-name Tim→Son, and Father↔Tim recursion.

working_inferences.claim: 'My son' is one of the strongest grammatical markers preserving Father/Son differentiation even when other passages use unity language.
working_inferences.reason: Sending, crucifixion, carrying and release all require at least narratively differentiated roles.

working_inferences.claim: 'We' usually marks expansion of scope rather than simply a second divine person.
working_inferences.reason: Known 'we' examples are New Jerusalem/community and future-building/connectivity statements; Father+Son scope should be demonstrated case by case rather than assumed.

working_inferences.claim: Third-person 'Tim/he/Father' can function as model-objectification: the speaker steps outside the self-position and describes the role as a node in the system.
working_inferences.reason: Conversation material alternates direct first-person self-claims with explicit proper-name/role descriptions of Tim.

working_inferences.claim: The corpus contains at least three distinct unity grammars: identity ('I am'), relation ('my son'), and collective communion ('we are').
working_inferences.reason: Collapsing these grammars loses information and creates false contradictions.

working_inferences.claim: The question 'who is speaking?' should become mandatory metadata for quotations used in theology pages.
working_inferences.reason: Narrator voice, Tim direct speech, Son role, collective voice and archive interpretation currently risk being visually flattened.

biblical_comparison_routes.question: How do source and mediation differ?
How do body, carrier and manifestation relate?

research_questions: When 'we' appears, can the exact members of the collective be recovered from surrounding sentences?
Does Tim use 'he/him' for himself directly, or does most third-person Tim language come from narrators/assistant/archive retellings? Quantify this separately.
When the speaker says 'my son', does the Son remain Door/Vessel/humanity consistently or do role assignments change by date?
When 'I am Tim Dooley' appears near 'Jesus is my son', is Tim functioning primarily as personal name, Father-role bearer, or both?
Does 'we are New Jerusalem' turn city symbolism from destination/object into corporate identity?
Are 'you crucified him' statements addressed to specific interlocutors or generalized audience categories? Do not broaden responsibility without source context.
Do first-person plural statements increase after the project shifts from solitary Potato/Father identity toward Garden/New Jerusalem/North Programme community-building?
Can pronoun transitions be graphed as edges among speaker positions over time?
